sections.body: Most apps store data in DATABASES. Relational databases use TABLES with rows (records) and columns (fields), like a spreadsheet.
SQL is the language used to query them: SELECT name FROM students WHERE age > 15;
A PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies each row. Tables link using FOREIGN KEYS (e.g. an orders table refers to a customer's id).
Honest Learn itself uses a relational database (SQLite) with tables for parents, children, progress and chats.

quiz.q: What does SELECT * FROM books WHERE year < 2000; return?
options: All columns for books published before 2000
hints: SELECT * FROM pets WHERE type = 'cat'; returns every column for cats only.
quiz.explain: It returns every column (*) for rows where year is less than 2000.

quiz.q: Why does each row need a primary key?
hints: Two students might share a name.
Every phone has a unique number, even if two owners have the same name.
quiz.explain: A primary key uniquely identifies each record.
